establishment.name: FLIK  INTERNATIONAL AT INOVA COMMONS CAFE

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. The food employee a The Grill was away from his work area. When he returned, he put on gloves and went back to work preparing food for customers. He did not wash his hands upon his return, as required.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS discussed this with the PIC and the employee.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided at the handsink in the kitchen and the one in the large dishwashing room.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The PIC corrected each of these during the inspection.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no handsoap available at the handsink at The Hearth pizza prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. FLIK INTERNATIONAL AT INOVA COMMONS CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/10/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: a container of raw salmon was stored over ready to eat cold cuts in the main walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: salmon on The Market hot rail was 128º. Salmon in The Market hot holding unit was 125º.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The PIC explained that the salmon is not hot because it is not covered while in the hot holding unit due to a quality issue. The salmon is typically served well before 4 hours, as the serving period is from 11:00 am to 2:30 pm daily. Try to keep the salmon 135º and above while in hot holding units. Storing the salmon on the top shelves of the hot holding unit might help since that area is hotter than others.

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: a container of jalapeños in The Hearth upright refrigerator had an expiration date of 7/24/26, which is several days (18) past the expiration date.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. The PIC discarded the jalapeños during the inspection.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided at the hand sink in the kitchen, air washing area. The paper towel dispenser in the large ware washing room was not working, so paper towels were not available.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The PIC corrected both issues during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the grill being used to store a wiping cloth sanitizer bucket.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The food employee moved the bucket during the inspection to correct. CDI.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: The hot water at the handwashing sink at the chef‘s table is 76°F.
violations.corrective_action: Hot water at a hand sink must be at least 100°F. There is most likely a mixing valve installed at this hand sink. Please have maintenance adjust the mixing valve so that hot water at the sink is at at least 100°F. This must be corrected within 10 days. Please notify the EHS when corrected.

out_items.name: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

violations.title: Package Integrity
violations.observation: The following food item(s) from damaged packaging were found offered for sale or service: a severely dented can of sliced ripe olives was located in the dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Food packages such as canned goods shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants. Return all dented and damaged canned goods to your food supplier for a credit. The PIC removed the can from the dry storage area and placed it in the segregated area. CDI.

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Written Procedures
violations.observation: Raw chicken, and raw flank steak were being prepared with a non-continuous cook process. The products were placed on the grill to create grill marks, then cooled, with complete cooking to take place later in the day. The PIC did not have written procedures for this process.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be prepared and stored according to written procedures that have obtained approval from the regulatory authority, are maintained in the food establishment and are available to the regulatory authority upon request, describe hot the requirements are to be monitored and documented and corrective actions taken, describe how the foods are to be marked as foods that must be further cooked, describe how the foods are to be separated from ready-to-eat foods. Please create and share written procedures for a non-continuous cook process for any foods being cooked this way with the EHS within 10 days.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed cooked steaks and chicken stored covered in the walk-in to cool.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. In order to cool foods rapidly do not cover them. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. CDI.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: there was no thermometer located in the display case with chicken Caesar salad in other foods in it.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. The PIC installed a thermometer in this unit during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: the food employee was storing a spatula for avocados on the hand sink at the grill station
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The employee moved the spatula during the visit and had it cleaned the EHS discussed that food equipment should not be stored on a hand sink. CDI. FLIK INTERNATIONAL AT INOVA COMMONS CAFE (Inspection Date: 02/13/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: door handles on the deli area refrigerator had food debris on them and were in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Please clean the refrigerator door handles daily.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Design Features
violations.observation: The backflow or backsiphonage prevention device installed on the mop sinks faucet (a splitter valve) in both ware washing areas were not an approved type and not identified as meeting standards set by the American Society of Sanitary Engineering.
violations.corrective_action: A backflow or back siphonage prevention device installed on a water supply system shall meet American Society of Sanitary Engineering (A.S.S.E.) standards for construction, installation, maintenance, inspection, and testing for that specific application and type of device. The EHS provide provided the PIC with a suitable alternative for the splitter install installed, at both the mop sinks, a Hydro systems 1951 pressure bleed dual valve unit. PIC said he would have maintenance order and install the devices and removed the unapproved splitters during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observe a significant amount of dust on the piping in the hood system, which could fall into food while being prepared. The rest of the hood system was basically clean.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Please have maintenance staff clean the dust off the piping as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: observed half and half at coffee bar (45F).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC time marked item and will discard half and half after 4 hours.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink (sink at dish washing area).
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. Paper towels were provided.

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Written Procedures
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not prepared and stored according to written procedures: Facility cooks chicken using a non-continuous cooking process, but does not have a variance for this process.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be prepared and stored according to written procedures that have obtained approval from the regulatory authority, are maintained in the food establishment and are available to the regulatory authority upon request, describe how the requirements are to be monitored and documented and corrective actions taken, describe how the foods are to be marked as foods that must be further cooked, describe how the foods are to be separated from ready-to-eat foods. Discontinue using the non-continuous cooking process. If it is desired to keep using this process, please submit a variance request via the PLUS system. This process should not be used without an approved variance.
